items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: I think he was really the HEIFETZ (PHONETIC) of the tenor saxophone.

ctx.x: But Ben had his thing he could do great. I mean, he was a great ballad player. You couldn't take that away from him. And Hawk could play everything. But Don Byas, I think, shot a little bit above both of them because he could do

everything and he had the finesse that neither Ben nor Hawk had. And I think he was really the HEIFETZ (PHONETIC) of the tenor saxophone. And anyway they all were great and I respected them all very much. And I have tapes on all of them. I have about 15 hours of Hawk, I have about 10 hours of Don Byas, I have about five or six hours of Ben. And there's a new album out I'm getting ready to get now that is just exported in. In fact, Ben and I were like brothers because his grandmother used to have a restaurant in…

She used to make pies and I loved strawberry pie. And she used to make me a whole pie. And I would get a quart of milk and sit there and eat it and wouldn't give Ben any of it. And he never would forget it. Years later he always said, he called me Bull and I named him Frog. And he would say, she made Bull a whole pie. He never did forget that.
